 Stormy set up Sunday through Monday with flooding possible
 Numerous thunderstorms Sunday and Monday with the risk for flooding. 
 Prev 
 Next 
 By: 
 Kate Wentzel 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add WPTV as a Google Preferred Source 
 WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — Look for widespread showers and storms Sunday with a 70% chance of rain. 
 A developing upper-level disturbance will support periods of showers and thunderstorms, with the potential for locally heavy rainfall.
 WPTV First Alert Weather Forecast for Night of Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 
 MORE WEATHER: Radar | Alerts | 7-Day Forecast | Hourly Forecast 
 SHORT-TERM FORECAST (SUNDAY – MONDAY) 
 The unsettled weather pattern is expected to become more pronounced Sunday into Monday. An approaching upper-level disturbance will help enhance upward motion across the Florida Peninsula, supporting more widespread shower and thunderstorm development.
 Sunday currently appears to be the wettest day of the forecast period, with numerous showers and thunderstorms possible throughout the day. Some storms could produce periods of heavy rainfall, frequent lightning, and localized flooding, particularly in areas that receive repeated rounds of precipitation.
 Rainfall amounts of 1–3 inches are possible across portions of South Florida, with locally higher totals where heavier downpours develop.
 By Monday, showers and thunderstorms are expected to remain in the forecast, although coverage may gradually become more scattered later in the day.
 EXTENDED OUTLOOK (TUESDAY – WEDNESDAY) 
 Conditions should begin to gradually improve by Tuesday, although lingering moisture will continue to support scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms.
 By Wednesday, a noticeable decrease in rain chances is expected as drier conditions begin to work into the region. Sunshine should become more prevalent, with afternoon temperatures returning to the middle 80s.
 COASTAL CONDITIONS 
 Multiple beach hazards are in place for both the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches on Sunday. Elevated surf, dangerous rip currents, and minor to moderate coastal flooding will remain concerns. 
 A High Surf Advisory continues through Sunday evening for the entire area. A Coastal Flood Advisory also remains in effect through Sunday evening, with coastal flooding possible during high-tide cycles. High tide occurs at the Lake Worth Inlet at 1:09 in the afternoon. 
 Beach conditions could become dangerous, especially for swimmers and anyone entering the Atlantic waters. Residents and visitors are encouraged to follow beach safety guidance and avoid entering the water when dangerous conditions are present.
 MARINE FORECAST 
 Boating conditions across the local Atlantic waters are expected to deteriorate Sunday as easterly to northeasterly winds strengthen.
 Winds of 20–25 knots and seas building to 7–10 feet along portions of the Gulf Stream will create hazardous conditions for smaller vessels. Small Craft Advisories are in effect for portions of the local Atlantic waters.
 MORE WEATHER: Radar | Alerts | 7-Day Forecast | Hourly Forecast 
 OVERALL OUTLOOK 
The main weather story for West Palm Beach over the next several days will be increasing rainfall potential with widespread showers and thunderstorms.
 Monday looks to stay wet too with gradual improvement Tuesday and beyond.
